To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the SEP in multihop communication with regenerative relaying is a function of the number of hops, the fading severity on each hop, the signal constellation size, and the number of relay stations.

for M-ary QAM in the multihop scenario with regenerative relaying the average SEP in Nakagami fading channels is a function of the number of hops, the Nakagami-m parameters and the number of signal constellation points, but not a function of the average signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) per bit.
the symbol error probability (or the average bit error probability) of multihop transmission with regenerative relaying can be calculated analytically for any modulation scheme and any channel model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the performance of multistage relaying schemes in terms of symbol error probability.
the analysis of the performance of M-ary quadratue amplitude modulation (M- QAM) in multihop communication system with regenerative relay.
the performance analysis of multihop wireless communication systems with regenerating relays.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the average SEP of M- QAM in the multihop system decreases monotonically with the number of relays, which is in contrast to the average bit error probability of binary modulations, where the average BER is maximized for an optimum number of relays.
the performance of the multihop communication system is dominated by the weakest link in the system.

the performance of the M-QAM scheme in multihop communication is superior to that of the BPSK scheme in terms of the SEP, and the performance of the QAM scheme in multichannel communication is superior to the QPSK scheme in the same system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the average SEP is determined by a weighted sum of the individual SEP contributions from the different hops.
the SEP performance is significantly improved in comparison to the case of non-regenerative relays.

the average SEP of M-ary quadratature amplitude modulation (QAM) is analyzed in a multihop communication system with regenerative relaying, and an analytical closed-form expression for the average symbol error probabiliy is obtained in time-invariant AWGN channels as well as in slow, frequency flat fading channels.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the average SEP in multihop systems with regenerative relay stations can be significantly lower than that of single-hop systems with the same total transmission distance and the same average received SNR per bit.
the SEP of multihop systems with regenerative relay stations is not necessarily worse than in single-hop systems, but may even be better.

the average SEP in multihop systems with M-QAM can be accurately and efficiently computed by means of a simple closed-form formula, which can be easily implemented in a computer program or in a digital signal processor.
